chapter: Early records, Detroit and Prohibition-era nightlife
title: Small's cabaret as a hotbed of real jazz
summary: Small's on Fifth Avenue and 35th Street was his first cabaret, a sawdust cellar with great players like Freddie Douglas and Joe Williams and piano players watching the girls in mirrors.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Oh, Small's was the first cabaret I was ever in. That was when Small's was on 5th Avenue, 5th Avenue and 35th Street was Small's. That was just a cellar, in a way of speaking. A pretty big cellar. It had sawdust on the floor and you know, these red and white table cloths and candles. And then that was -- that was the hotbed of real jazz. That's where you had people down there who played more jazz than you ever heard in your life. People can talk all they want about who played jazz and who didn't.
Well, he had Elmer Snowd@n was there and Roy, and Rex Stewart.....

Even before that. I never heard of Elmer Snowd@n or Rex Stewart. They were people I -- Freddie Jenkins -- Freddie Douglas. Freddie Douglas, he was a great waw-waw, man. Joe Williams, the trombone player. A guy they called Jazz, he used to be a drummer. And all kinds of piano players you never even heard of. Oh, those piano players. You know, that's when a girl used to go from table to table, all around the floor, you know. These piano players would just sit there with a mirror over the piano, you know, looking in the mirror to see what the girls were doing with the money, you know. A cigarette hanging. Beautiful piano players, oh, jeez, I'm telling you.
